articleTitle: The application of variable message signs for traffic management and safety
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: The UK Department of Transport specification for a new generation of cantilever mounted light emitting signs soon to be commissioned on the M25 takes cognizance of three evaluation sites, research at Aston and Southampton Universities and developments in Europe. The visual impact of the enhanced message signals as they are termed will be better then reflective signs, but the real efficacy of the signs will be observed in adverse weather conditions when the emitted light will penetrate drizzle and fog. The Scottish Office has piloted a number of variable message signs (VMS) systems. Schemes in Borders and Grampian Regions advise motorists of diversionary routes, when snow has blocked mountain roads, perhaps the most comprehensive VMS systems so far installed in Britain are the two systems providing traffic management and driver information on the Forth Road Bridge and A90/M90 in Fife Region.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of a street lighting fault monitoring device
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: The circuit module was initially conceived to contain five elements namely: a sensing device to register the presence or absence of the electrical circuit characteristics; a module to contain a unique resident address code to identify the lighting unit from others in the area; a module to compare the received address with the resident address; a module to convert data from serial input to parallel use in the monitor and then returned to serial data for outward transmission; and a transmit/receiver radio module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Motorway widening-active management of road networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: Whilst motorway widening is being planned and executed, it is all too easy to become engrossed in the concrete, trenches, cables, transponders and so on. At times with any engineering task it is necessary to look forward, imagine what is being created, ask if it satisfies both the present needs and the needs of the future and explore exactly how it can be used to optimum effect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: Motorway lighting is a field where the continuing development of more effective, economical and efficient technology can be assumed. The need for motorway lighting is assessed, the performance requirements are defined, and some aspects of lighting design are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upgrading from NMCS1 to NMCS2 (motorway control systems)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: An upgrading exercise may take place under three circumstances. It may be a straightforward communications upgrade where there is already an existing 30 pair cable in situ. It may be carried out as part of a road widening contract when the communications are also re-equipped with a new cable infrastructure and new equipment. It may be an interim upgrade which takes place when an existing 20 pair installation is to be temporally used to operate a restricted NMCS2 service. These three possibilities are dealt with.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Median and verge lighting for wide motorways
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: Discusses the problems of median and verge lighting. The ultimate disadvantage of lighting from the verge would be increased installation costs, running costs, and glare. From the lighting designer's point of view it is better to light a motorway from the centre, but if ease of maintenance outweighs the efficiency of the lighting, then verge lighting with specifically designed luminaire becomes a possibility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Driver information on widened motorways trials of a new motorway signal on the M25
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: The signal combines an improved version of the traditional motorway indicator with a variable message sign (VMS) capable of displaying a wide range of information to the motorist. The new signal will not only be able to advise the motorist of speed restrictions, lane closures, diversions, etc, but will also indicate the reason for the restriction. In addition it will be used to give motorists warning of problems sufficient distance in advance of an incident to allow them to divert, if they so wish. It is anticipated that the additional driver information provided by the new signal will minimise queues and congestion, permitting more efficient use of the motorway, and increase the motorist's response to signals, thereby improving safety. The signal has been designed to integrate into the second generation National Motorway Communications System (NMCS II) and has been specified so that it can be used to assist in the overall management of the motorway/all purpose road network using techniques currently under development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: The proposals to widen some of the motorways will have a considerable impact on the National Motorway Communications System (NMCS). The scope of the MWU projects, the type of widening options and the completions timescales for some of the schemes poses a range of problems. One of the most significant is the possible introduction of a new range of signals and their relevant provision/design standards, and how they would integrate with the fixed signs. Overall system design and maintenance of existing facilities during works programmes is also likely to create significant problems. The paper outlines the extent of the MWU programme, and considers some aspects of signalling at junctions/interchanges on D4 motorways. It also briefly discusses system design, maintenance of existing facilities and the techniques to improve signal setting response with the help of automatic incident detection (AID) and CCTV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: NMC 2, the UK Department of Transport's National Motorway Communication System-Mark Two is nowadays attracting a considerable amount of overseas interest. As authorities around the world recognise the need for sophisticated control and communications systems on their freeways, the availability of a system 'off-the-shelf', with expansion capability designed in, is proving very attractive. The paper shows how that expansion capability has been utilised in the provision of a system for the M30 motorway around Madrid. It also outlines how additional applications could be handled, with a minimum of alteration to the standard system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote device radio communications system for NMCSII
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: Serco Systems Limited are currently developing for the UK Department of Transport (DOT) a prototype system for the control of variable message signs (VMS), using the Paknet public radio data communications service. The system under development is being designed not only for the control of VMS in remote areas but also to meet the requirements of the DOT's specification TR 2067. This specification relates to the standard RS485 Communications protocols and data formats for the National Motorways Communication System II (NMCSII). The developments described resulted from a revision to the system techniques forming part of Serco's contract with the DOT for the supply of control equipment for the traffic management systems on the approaches to the new Dartford-Thurrock Bridge River Crossing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motorway Widening: Opportunities for New Communications and Lighting
abstract: The lighting of wide motorways requires the use of special techniques and equipment, which differ in many ways from those applied to conventional road lighting. The paper attempts to highlight these differences and to examine the fundamental technical aspects of the luminaries and applications currently conceived. Energy efficiency and environmental considerations are also included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
